title: My Morning and Evening
intro: Ten source-grounded lessons for beginning and ending the day with remembrance, praise, trust, gratitude and care for others. Short phrases lead gradually to longer morning-and-evening supplications and a Qur’an recitation routine.
reviewStatus: Working curriculum text copied verbatim from the supplied DOCX. Qualified scholarly, Arabic, Urdu and pronunciation review is required before release.

lessons.title: A New Morning, A New Gift
lessons.tagline: VOLUME 07 / PROPHETIC MORNING DU’A / GRATITUDE FOR A NEW DAY

words.text: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا وَبِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا وَبِكَ نَحْيَا وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ وَإِلَيْكَ النُّشُورُ
Allāhumma bika aṣbaḥnā wa bika amsaynā wa bika naḥyā wa bika namūtu wa ilaykan-nushūr.

words.label: English meaning

blocks.text: Abu Hurayrah (RA) reported morning and evening wordings from the Prophet ﷺ. This is the complete morning form as recorded in Abi Dawud 5068; do not merge it with a different collection’s form.

story: Morning sunlight reached the curtains in Amanpur. Akhlaq was still sleepy, and Imaan was getting her schoolbag ready. Salaam greeted them warmly and said, “A new day is a gift.” Together they listened to a morning Du’a. Akhlaq repeated the short parts without rushing while Imaan pointed to the words on the screen. Then they prepared their bags and helped make the breakfast table ready. The Du’a gave their morning a gentle and purposeful beginning.
understand: These words remind us that life, time and the final return to Allah are in His control. A good morning does not mean everything must be perfect; it means we begin with remembrance, gratitude and a willingness to do good. It is a morning supplication—not a general promise that today will be free from problems.

lessons.action: Begin one morning this week by reciting this Du’a with a family member before starting your activities.

mission.title: The morning window
mission.feedback: A peaceful beginning can include remembrance and a kind action.

blocks.text: The same Abu Hurayrah (RA) narration preserves a separate evening wording. Here the cited Arabic ends with وَإِلَيْكَ النُّشُورُ; some other collections transmit a different ending, so the app must not splice the variants.

story: After their evening activities, Imaan and Akhlaq sat beside Salamah as the sky grew dim. They had both enjoyed parts of their day and made small mistakes too. Salamah reminded them that another chance to learn would come tomorrow, in shaa Allah. She played the evening Du’a. Akhlaq noticed that it was similar to the morning one, but the beginning was different. Imaan practised the evening words carefully, and together they remembered Allah before returning to their family tasks.
understand: The morning and evening Du’as are related but not identical. Learn the wording for each occasion without accidentally replacing one with the other. The evening remembrance is an opportunity to remember Allah and be grateful, not a test of whether the day was successful.

lessons.title: Seeking Allah’s Protection Each Day
lessons.tagline: VOLUME 07 / PROPHETIC MORNING-AND-EVENING DHIKR / FAITH WITH SENSIBLE CARE

words.text: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
Bismillāhilladhī lā yaḍurru maʿa ismihi shay’un fil-arḍi wa lā fis-samā’i wa huwas-Samīʿul-ʿAlīm.

words.label: English meaning
words.text: In the name of Allah, with Whose name nothing in the earth or heaven can cause harm; He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
اللہ کے نام سے، جس کے نام کے ساتھ زمین اور آسمان کی کوئی چیز نقصان نہیں پہنچا سکتی، اور وہ سب کچھ سننے والا، سب کچھ جاننے والا ہے۔

words.label: When to recite
words.text: Morning and evening; the reported count is three times on each occasion.

words.label: Reported Sunnah repetition
words.text: 3 times in the morning; 3 times in the evening

words.label: Primary source and status
words.text: Sunan Abi Dawud 5088 — Sahih (al-Albani)
https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5088

blocks.text: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān (RA) narrated the report through Abān ibn ʿUthmān. It contains a reported threefold count and the account of Abān’s illness. Avoid claiming that children can never be injured or ill.

story: Akhlaq wanted to hurry outside to play. Salaam reminded him to put on his shoes and check that the garden path was clear. Imaan helped him remember the morning Dhikr they had started learning. “We ask Allah for protection,” said Salaam, “and we also use the safety advice He has allowed us to learn.” The children listened to each phrase, repeated it together, and then went outdoors while following their family’s safety rules.
understand: This authentic remembrance is taught for morning and evening, three times on each occasion. It expresses trust in Allah’s protection. The Hadith should be presented respectfully and accurately, while avoiding statements such as “If you say this, nothing bad can ever happen.” We still use road safety, medical care and adult supervision.

mission.feedback: Remember Allah and take wise precautions.

words.text: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
Subḥānallāhi wa biḥamdih.

words.label: English meaning
words.text: Glory and perfection belong to Allah, and praise belongs to Him.
اللہ ہر عیب سے پاک ہے اور اسی کے لیے تمام تعریف ہے۔

words.label: When to recite
words.text: Morning and evening; one hundred times at each occasion in the cited report.

words.label: Reported Sunnah repetition
words.text: 100 times in the morning; 100 times in the evening

words.label: Primary source and status
words.text: Sahih Muslim 2692
https://sunnah.com/muslim:2692

lessons.english: Glory and perfection belong to Allah, and praise belongs to Him.
lessons.urdu: اللہ ہر عیب سے پاک ہے اور اسی کے لیے تمام تعریف ہے۔
lessons.occasion: Morning and evening; one hundred times at each occasion in the cited report.

blocks.text: Abu Hurayrah (RA) transmitted the Prophet’s ﷺ teaching about this Dhikr in the morning and evening. The Arabic phrase is short, but the Sunnah count is substantial; younger children may build up with family help.

story: Dadi Jaan was sorting buttons into a small box when Akhlaq asked why there were so many. She smiled. “Sometimes small things, done carefully, add up.” She taught the children the short Dhikr “Subḥānallāhi wa biḥamdih.” Imaan practised the two phrases until they sounded familiar. Akhlaq counted his first few repetitions on his fingers and rested. Nobody rushed him. Dadi Jaan explained that the authentic narration mentions one hundred repetitions in the morning and evening, and learning can happen step by step.
understand: The words are brief, and the Hadith reports a count of one hundred each morning and evening. This religious count must stay distinct from optional app practice settings. For an early learner, hearing, pronouncing and remembering the phrase correctly may be the immediate educational target. Never shame a child who is not yet ready to complete a long count.
lessons.memorizeSteps: Listen to qualified Arabic audio, repeat the segments, reconnect them in order, and try gentle audio-only recall. The reported Sunnah count is not the same as the user-adjustable sound-loop count.
lessons.action: Practise this Dhikr with a parent at an achievable pace today, remembering the authentic one-hundred-count goal without rushing.

mission.text: Offer a calm, accessible count interface with pause/resume, no time limit, and a separate memorization-practice counter; do not award more holiness points for higher counts.
mission.title: The quiet Dhikr counter
mission.feedback: Slow, steady remembrance is worth practising.

lessons.reflect: How do I feel when I do something good patiently?

guidance.text: Support the Sunnah count faithfully while letting children learn gradually; no reward for unlimited tapping or device time.

blocks.text: Thawbān (RA) narrated this evening remembrance. The exact Tirmidhi wording does NOT contain a threefold repetition instruction. Abu Dawud 5072 is separately graded weak by al-Albani; do not use its grading silently to upgrade this entry.

story: At the end of a busy day, Imaan was putting her books away when Akhlaq asked why they had a special time for remembering Allah. Salamah replied, “We have been given faith, and we can be thankful for it.” The family learned a short remembrance about being pleased with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muhammad ﷺ as Prophet. Imaan repeated each part while Akhlaq matched the words to their meanings. They spoke respectfully about what the words meant to them.
understand: These words are a statement of contentment with one’s faith. The exact cited Tirmidhi report links the phrase to evening remembrance and labels it Hasan Gharib. We should not quietly attach the “three times each morning and evening” claim to this particular narration. The practical lesson is grateful commitment, not superiority over other children.

lessons.action: Say this remembrance in the evening and show respect to someone who has a different opinion or background.

mission.text: Match Rabb, Dīn and Nabī to the corresponding child-friendly meanings, then play the complete Arabic without a countdown.
mission.title: Three meanings, one remembrance
mission.feedback: You are learning both the words and their meaning.

lessons.title: Thankful for My Health and Senses
lessons.tagline: VOLUME 07 / PROPHETIC MORNING-AND-EVENING DU’A / GRATITUDE, CARE AND KINDNESS

words.text: اللَّهُمَّ عَافِنِي فِي بَدَنِي، اللَّهُمَّ عَافِنِي فِي سَمْعِي، اللَّهُمَّ عَافِنِي فِي بَصَرِي، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
Allāhumma ʿāfinī fī badanī; Allāhumma ʿāfinī fī samʿī; Allāhumma ʿāfinī fī baṣarī; lā ilāha illā Anta.

words.label: English meaning
words.text: O Allah, grant well-being to my body, hearing and sight. There is no deity worthy of worship except You.
اے اللہ! میرے جسم، سماعت اور بینائی کو عافیت عطا فرما۔ تیرے سوا کوئی معبود برحق نہیں۔

words.label: When to recite
words.text: Morning and evening; Abu Bakrah (RA) described repeating this set three times at each time.

words.label: Reported Sunnah repetition
words.text: 3 times in the morning; 3 times in the evening

words.label: Primary source and status
words.text: Sunan Abi Dawud 5090 — Hasan in chain (al-Albani)
https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5090

lessons.transliteration: Allāhumma ʿāfinī fī badanī; Allāhumma ʿāfinī fī samʿī; Allāhumma ʿāfinī fī baṣarī; lā ilāha illā Anta.
lessons.english: O Allah, grant well-being to my body, hearing and sight. There is no deity worthy of worship except You.

lessons.occasion: Morning and evening; Abu Bakrah (RA) described repeating this set three times at each time.
lessons.source: Sunan Abi Dawud 5090 — Hasan in chain (al-Albani)

blocks.text: Abū Bakrah (RA) explained to his son that he had heard the Prophet ﷺ use these words; the account mentions three repetitions. This lesson teaches the first health-related set; the same report contains other supplications which are not silently merged here.

story: Imaan was thankful she could read the day’s lesson, and Akhlaq enjoyed hearing birds from the window. But their class had children with many different abilities. Salamah taught them that we can ask Allah for well-being while respecting everyone. She played the morning-and-evening Du’a for health, hearing and sight. The children practised one line at a time, then talked about helping classmates use the tools and support they need. They learned that gratitude should make us kinder, never proud.
understand: The Du’a asks Allah for well-being in body, hearing and sight and affirms His oneness. It is not a judgment on people living with disabilities; their dignity and worth are equal. Children can learn to appreciate blessings without assuming that illness is punishment or that prayer replaces professional care.
lessons.memorizeSteps: Listen to qualified Arabic audio, repeat the segments, reconnect them in order, and try gentle audio-only recall. The reported Sunnah count is not the same as the user-adjustable sound-loop count.
lessons.action: Offer one kind, respectful act to someone today without making assumptions about their abilities.

mission.text: Learn the four phrases by sound, match body/hearing/sight to neutral icons, then pick an inclusive way to help a friend.
mission.title: The blessings garden
mission.feedback: Gratitude grows when we treat others with respect.

lessons.reflect: How can I be thankful for my abilities and kind to everyone?

guidance.text: Avoid disability as a “bad ending,” and avoid asking children to disclose personal health information.

lessons.title: Three Surahs for Morning and Evening
lessons.tagline: VOLUME 07 / QUR’ANIC RECITATION PRESCRIBED IN MORNING AND EVENING / TRUST IN ALLAH AND CONSISTENCY

words.text:
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ۝ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ ۝ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ ۝ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ

قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ ۝ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ

قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ ۝ مَلِكِ النَّاسِ ۝ إِلَٰهِ النَّاسِ ۝ مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ ۝ الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ ۝ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ
Read the full three surahs from verified Qur’anic audio; do not substitute a brief phonetic line for Qur’anic recitation.

words.label: English meaning
words.text: Surah Al-Ikhlas teaches the oneness of Allah; Al-Falaq and An-Nas teach us to seek refuge in Allah from harm and evil whispers. Full verse-by-verse meanings belong in the linked Qur’an module.
سورۃ الاخلاص اللہ تعالیٰ کی وحدانیت سکھاتی ہے، جبکہ سورۃ الفلق اور سورۃ الناس میں ہم اللہ کی پناہ مانگنا سیکھتے ہیں۔ مکمل ترجمہ متعلقہ قرآنی ماڈیول میں ہوگا۔

words.label: When to recite
words.text: Recite each of the three complete surahs three times in the morning and three times in the evening.

words.label: Reported Sunnah repetition

lessons.arabic:
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ۝ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ ۝ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ ۝ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ

قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ ۝ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ

قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ ۝ مَلِكِ النَّاسِ ۝ إِلَٰهِ النَّاسِ ۝ مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ ۝ الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ ۝ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ
lessons.english: Surah Al-Ikhlas teaches the oneness of Allah; Al-Falaq and An-Nas teach us to seek refuge in Allah from harm and evil whispers. Full verse-by-verse meanings belong in the linked Qur’an module.
lessons.urdu: سورۃ الاخلاص اللہ تعالیٰ کی وحدانیت سکھاتی ہے، جبکہ سورۃ الفلق اور سورۃ الناس میں ہم اللہ کی پناہ مانگنا سیکھتے ہیں۔ مکمل ترجمہ متعلقہ قرآنی ماڈیول میں ہوگا۔
lessons.occasion: Recite each of the three complete surahs three times in the morning and three times in the evening.

extras.heading: COMPLETE SURAH MEANINGS • REVIEW WITH THE QUR’AN MODULE

blocks.text: Al-Ikhlas 112:1–4 (English):  Say: Allah is One; Allah is the One upon Whom all depend. He neither has children nor was born, and no one is equal to Him.
کہہ دیجیے: اللہ ایک ہے، اللہ سب سے بے نیاز ہے، نہ اس کی کوئی اولاد ہے اور نہ وہ کسی کی اولاد ہے، اور کوئی اس کے برابر نہیں۔

Al-Falaq 113:1–5 (English):  Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak from the evil of what He created; from the darkness when it deepens; from those who blow on knots; and from an envier when envy is acted upon.
کہہ دیجیے: میں صبح کے رب کی پناہ مانگتا ہوں، اس کی مخلوق کے شر سے، چھا جانے والی تاریکی کے شر سے، گرہوں میں پھونکنے والوں کے شر سے، اور حسد کرنے والے کے شر سے جب وہ حسد کرے۔

An-Nas 114:1–6 (English):  Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of humanity, the King of humanity, the God of humanity, from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws, who whispers into human hearts, whether from jinn or humans.

کہہ دیجیے: میں لوگوں کے رب، لوگوں کے بادشاہ، لوگوں کے معبود کی پناہ مانگتا ہوں، اس وسوسہ ڈالنے والے کے شر سے جو پیچھے ہٹ جاتا ہے، جو لوگوں کے دلوں میں وسوسے ڈالتا ہے، خواہ وہ جنوں میں سے ہو یا انسانوں میں سے۔

ʿAbdullāh ibn Khubayb (RA) narrated the Prophet’s ﷺ instruction to recite Surah Al-Ikhlas and the two Muʿawwidhatayn three times in morning and evening. The full Arabic here is Qur’anic text, not a literal quote of all the verses from the Hadith.

story: Akhlaq had learned Surah Al-Ikhlas in his Qur’an lessons, but he was unsure why the family recited it alongside two other short surahs. Imaan opened the Qur’an module and saw Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas in order. They listened with Salamah and practised each surah separately. When Akhlaq forgot a word, he replayed the correct portion rather than guessing. Soon, he could join the family’s morning recitation at a comfortable pace.
understand: This lesson links the Du’a journey to the separate Qur’an memorization journey. These are complete Qur’anic surahs, not ordinary spoken Du’a texts. Their authentic morning/evening recitation count is three times each. Display full approved Uthmani text, verified verse numbers and qualified recitation audio; no “magic shield” animation or claims that ordinary safety can be ignored.

lessons.action: With a parent or teacher, practise reciting Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas in the correct order during one morning or evening.

blocks.text: Ibn ʿUmar (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ regularly used these Du’as in morning and evening. The source carries a singular/plural variant concerning ʿawrah; this entry uses the plural wording noted in ʿUthmān’s version, including وَآمِنْ رَوْعَاتِي.

story: Before leaving for a family visit, Akhlaq noticed that Salamah was checking the bags and reminding everyone where to meet if they became separated. “Are we worried?” he asked. “We plan carefully,” she explained, “and we also ask Allah for well-being.” She showed the children a longer Du’a for protection, family and safety. Imaan learned its first sentence that day. Akhlaq listened to the next one. They decided to take their time rather than try to memorize all the words at once.
understand: This comprehensive supplication asks Allah for protection, well-being and forgiveness in many areas of life. It includes adult concepts such as privacy, fear and harm; explain these gently as dignity, safety and asking Allah to care for us. It does not replace sensible family plans or emergency instructions. Preserve the selected wording variant as an approved unit.

blocks.text: Abu Bakr al-Siddīq (RA) asked the Prophet ﷺ for words to say in the morning and evening. The Prophet ﷺ taught this supplication and also instructed it before lying down. The Arabic uses the Abu Dawud 5067 arrangement, which differs in order from Tirmidhi 3392.

story: Imaan and Akhlaq were looking at the clear sky from their home. Akhlaq wondered how many stars existed beyond what he could see. Dadi Jaan explained that Allah knows all things, including what is hidden from us. Then she shared a Du’a that the Prophet ﷺ taught Abu Bakr (RA). The children listened to its first two phrases and learned that Allah created the heavens and earth. Their curiosity made them eager to ask questions—and their Du’a reminded them to ask Allah for help in making good choices.
understand: This is a beautiful combination of Allah’s greatness, Tawḥīd and seeking protection from one’s own wrong inclinations and Shaytan. Children need not be frightened by the unseen. Teach the words with calm explanation and a verified audio sequence; keep the historical teaching to Abu Bakr (RA) separate from the fictional Amanpur setting.

story: The family had returned home after visiting relatives. Akhlaq was ready to play, while Imaan wanted to finish a drawing. Dadi Jaan invited them for a short evening remembrance. “This one is longer,” she said, “so we will learn it in parts.” Imaan repeated the opening line. Akhlaq repeated the praise of Allah. They listened to the remaining phrases before continuing their activities. Over several evenings, the words became familiar. The family valued careful learning rather than speed.
understand: This longer evening remembrance includes praise of Allah, affirmation of His oneness, prayer for good during the night and refuge from many forms of harm and spiritual trial. Some later phrases are not immediately easy for younger children; provide age-appropriate explanations and allow assisted listening. No dramatic fear scenes, predictions or invented fixed repetition count.
